title: SaffronAI POC week 3 throughput & cost handoff
summary: Week 3 POC review focusing on tokens/sec per dollar, cache hit improvements, batching tradeoffs, and next validation steps toward pilot sign-off.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (CSM) — Lina, Raj, Diane, Omar (SaffronAI)
Shared: throughput spreadsheet (link: /saffron/poc/throughput.xlsx), security checklist doc (link shared in chat)

Summary (auto): quick recap of week-3 numbers, cache hit improvements (~15% -> 62%), tokens/sec per dollar uplift from batching and prefix caching; decisions on next 48h validation run and quantization test matrix.

[00:00:08] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, I'll kick us off. quick agenda — results, tuning changes we made yesterday, and next steps for the 48 hour validation run.
[00:00:22] Lina: yea thanks Maya. we got the sheet open. excited to see the numbers.
[00:00:28] Ethan: cool, so i'll share screen for one sec — sorry if audio lags. so first slide, tokens per dollar, we're measuring tokens/sec per dollar at the request shape you gave us (avg prompt ~420 tokens, avg gen 230 tokens) so that combined typical turn is ~650 tokens.
[00:00:48] Raj: quick clar — tokens/sec per dollar, is that normalized across model variants? are we comparing the quantized 4-bit to fp16?
[00:00:56] Ethan: good question. yes the main baseline in the sheet is the float16 family endpoint (redwood-gpt-13b-fp16) then we have projected 4-bit quantized numbers. the live POC runs on 8-bit q8 as we agreed for parity.
[00:01:12] Diane: I'm just scanning the caching row — earlier you said cache hit was low, what's the improvement story?
[00:01:18] Maya: right, we instrumented prefix caching and bumped TTL for the conversational prefix. initial hit rate was 15% on day 1, after we added the conversation-level keying and increased the prefix window we saw it jump to about 62% in the last 24 hours.
[00:01:36] Omar: 62% seems high, is that on all traffic or only the sampled test traffic?
[00:01:40] Ethan: it's weighted — 62% on the test corpus that's close to production prompts; overall traffic is at 48% because of some long-tail prompts. remember the cache only saves generation cost, not prompt tokens.
[00:01:54] Lina: ok san — sorry, can you spell that out? does that mean costs dropped by 62%?
[00:02:00] Maya: no, not cost drop. cache hit rate is percent of requests that reused KV cache so the per-token generation compute was lower for those. net effect for the mixed workload is about 27% reduction in tokens/sec-dollar cost so far.
[00:02:14] Raj: can you show the math quickly?
[00:02:17] Ethan: sure. baseline tokens/sec/$ with no cache and 8-bit q is 1,240 tokens/sec per dollar (empirical on our nodes for this profile). with 48% effective cache hit and a 0.35x generation cost when cache hit (we're reusing k/v for prefix) the weighted tokens/sec/$ becomes roughly 1,240 * (1 - 0.48 + 0.48/0.35) — gives the net ~1,580 tokens/sec/$, so about +27%. numbers in sheet, tab "econ calc".
[00:02:50] Lina: hmm that helps. the business asks for tokens per dollar and tokens per second because we're capacity planning — are you also tracking tail latency?
[00:02:59] Ethan: yes, tail p95/p99 did creep up when we increased batching, here's the tradeoff that came up.
[00:03:05] [00:03:05] Ethan: with aggressive batching (batch size 64, wait 12ms) throughput improves 30% but p99 adds ~120ms for small requests; with smaller batching (size 16, wait 4ms) throughput lower but latency stable.
[00:03:20] Raj: For our product we need sub-400ms p95 for interactive features — can we hit tokens/sec/$ improvements without breaking that?
[00:03:28] Maya: yes the recommendation is dynamic batching policy: route interactive routes to latency-priority pool (batch cap 16) and background summarization/analytics to throughput pool (batch cap 64). config is already in the toggle file we shared.
[00:03:44] Lina: and that requires dedicated capacity? or can hosted do that routing?
[00:03:49] Ethan: hosted can do it with fine-grained routing and policy — you get multi-pool routing but for stricter isolation and guaranteed latency you'd go dedicated. for the POC we showed both, hosted with QoS and a dedicated node set.
[00:04:02] Omar: any note about KV cache consistency across pools? if we route to a different pool we lose the local cache.
[00:04:07] Ethan: correct, cache is local to serving pool. that's why we recommend session-affinity routing for interactive sessions — same user sticky to same pool for short TTLs.
[00:04:18] Diane: small heads-up — product wants to avoid session stickiness where possible because of multi-region users.
[00:04:24] Maya: understood, tradeoffs — sticky routing increases cache hit and lowers cost but can impact geo-availability. one mitigation is global prefix sync (cold-sync) but it increases sync overhead.
[00:04:36] Lina: can you run an experiment that simulates our multi-region traffic with and without stickiness?
[00:04:41] Maya: yes, next steps include a 48-hour run that simulates your 40% multi-region tail and we will toggle stickiness.
[00:04:51] Raj: on quantization — you mentioned a 4-bit path that might save more than batching, what's the risk to quality?
[00:04:58] Ethan: we ran a short eval against your eval set (shared in repo) — 4-bit quant (GPT-13b-4bit-ptq) shows minimal BLEU/rouge shift on your prompts but hallucination patterns need closer checks. we put a regression flag if rouge drops >2.5 points.
[00:05:15] Lina: were there any specific prompt families that degraded?
[00:05:18] Ethan: long-chain reasoning prompts had higher variance, and very long instructions with nested lists. we'll add targeted evals for those.
[00:05:26] Diane: are those evals automated in the pipeline? we want daily guardrail checks.
[00:05:30] Jordan: yes we can hook the eval job into your CI or Redwood's eval harness; Jordan to coordinate.
[00:05:36] [00:05:36] Jordan: i'll drop a snippet in the shared doc for hooking into your CI.
[00:05:40] Lina: good.
[00:05:43] Maya: other operational note: we saw a throttling edge case when concurrency spikes >320 on a single node; Redwood autoscaling handled it but latencies spiked briefly.
[00:05:55] Raj: is that because of the backend QPS limiter or GPU saturation?
[00:05:58] Ethan: GPU saturation with small batch profiles, yes. autoscaler will add nodes but there's a small scale-up delay; mitigation is pre-warm or burst pool config. we recommended enabling burst capacity for peak windows.
[00:06:10] Lina: price for burst pool?
[00:06:12] Maya: burst is standard extra hourly add-on; we'll put exact numbers in the pricing sheet — estimated marginal cost for your peak is about +9% versus steady state.
[00:06:21] Omar: can we pin model versions to avoid silent rollout regressions?
[00:06:25] Ethan: yes, pinning supported; you can also set canary rollout with automatic rollback on eval regressions.
[00:06:31] Diane: great. ok so can we recap decisions?
[00:06:35] Maya: recap: 1) run 48h validation with multi-region sim and stickiness toggled; 2) run quantization matrix (8-bit q8 baseline, 4-bit PTQ candidate) on targeted eval buckets; 3) enable dynamic routing: interactive → latency pool, background → throughput pool; 4) enable burst capacity for peak windows; 5) Jordan will share CI eval integration snippet; Ethan will schedule benchmark run.
[00:06:57] Lina: good.
[00:07:00] [00:07:00] Raj: couple more clarifications on the caching math, is the 0.35x generation cost reduction a measured number or a model?
[00:07:07] Ethan: measured on our 80% prefix reuse microbenchmarks for that model arch. we will include confidence intervals in the sheet.
[00:07:15] Lina: product would like an executive slide: tokens/sec/$ improvement, expected delta to monthly bill, and latency SLO impacts.
[00:07:22] Maya: we'll produce that and target a short deck by tomorrow EOD.
[00:07:27] Omar: any security flags we should be aware of before running the 48h sim?
[00:07:31] Jordan: we've got the security checklist, SSO flow is configured and audit logs are enabled for the POC cluster. no open items except customer confirmation on retain logs duration.
[00:07:40] Lina: we want 90 days retention, is that compatible?
[00:07:43] Jordan: yes, default is 30 but we can extend for POC to 90. we'll note that.
[00:07:48] Diane: what are next steps timeline?
[00:07:50] Maya: immediate: Jordan and Ethan will kick off the 48h run tomorrow; deliverable: validation report + executive slide by Friday. quant matrix by Monday.
[00:08:01] Lina: ok thanks team.

[00:08:12] // end of recording notes: natural disfluencies, occasional speaker overlap.
action_items: Jordan Li|Share CI eval integration snippet and security retention config|2026-01-08
Ethan Ross|Kick off 48-hour multi-region throughput validation with stickiness toggles; attach raw logs and p95/p99 graphs|2026-01-09
Maya Patel|Prepare executive slide (tokens/sec/$ delta, expected monthly bill impact, latency SLO implication)|2026-01-09
Lina Cho|Confirm 90-day audit log retention for POC|2026-01-08
next_steps: 48-hour validation run with and without session stickiness (Ethan)
Quantization matrix testing across targeted eval buckets (Ethan & Saffron ML)
Adjust POC log retention to 90 days (Jordan)
